 Advertisement How many people early voted in Ohio, Kentucky, Indiana? A look at the data
 Advertisement Updated: 3:56 PM EST Nov 2, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Fletcher Keel Digital Editor How many people early voted in Ohio, Kentucky, Indiana? A look at the data
 Updated: 3:56 PM EST Nov 2, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Fletcher Keel Digital Editor Election Day is Tuesday, but millions of voters have already made their voices heard.
 Almost 55 million Americans have voted early this election cycle. Of that number, 24 million of them are mail-in ballots. The other 30 million were voters who voted early in-person.
 Advertisement Voters in Ohio, Kentucky and Indiana turned out in record numbers.
 In Ohio, more than 1.6 million people took advantage of early and absentee voting.
 That number was over 400,000 in Kentucky, more than 100,000 than who voted early in 2022.
 The latest data shows 803,437 people voted early in Indiana, compared to 606,040 in 2022.
 Zooming in even further, nearly 200,000 people have voted in Southwest Ohio, the majority of whom are older than 65. 
 If you didn't vote early, you can still cast your ballot on Tuesday during Election Day.
 Polls open in Kentucky and Indiana on Tuesday at 6 a.m., and will close at 6 p.m.
 In Ohio, polls will be open from 6:30 a.m. until 7:30 p.m.
